chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from Al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the Aqeeqa: when you slaughter, you should say:
I have turned my face toward Him who originated the heavens and the earth, upright and submitting.
And I am not of the polytheists.
Surely my Prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are (all) for Allah, the Lord of the worlds. There is no associate for Him.
O Allah, from You and for You.
O Allah, this is on behalf of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended words to recite when slaughtering an animal for Aqeeqa?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the ritual formula for Aqeeqa, blending the Prophet's declaration of pure monotheism (Hanif) with a specific dedication to the child. It reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating Quranic recitation directly into the physical act of sacrifice, linking the ritual to the broader theological concept of dedicating one's entire existence to Allah.
